🐉🇲🇽🌐 China reaffirms "firm support" for Mexico's sovereignty — deepens Strategic Partnership

Chinese Ambassador Chen Daojiang met Mexico's new Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez on May 16, reaffirming Beijing's "firm support" for Mexico's independence and autonomy.

Both sides agreed to deepen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — diplomatic language for structural, long-term cooperation. This comes as Ebrard prepares commercial missions to China and India before month's end, alongside the EU trade deal signing on May 22.

While Washington threatens tariffs and USMCA penalties, Beijing offers partnership. Mexico isn't choosing sides — it's multiplying options. Three trade fronts in one month: China, India, EU. That's what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar world.

🇲🇽🌎 MOSCOW AND BEIJING REJECT WORLD ORDER "WHERE ONLY FORCE PREVAILS"

Days after Trump left Beijing, Putin arrived — and he and Xi signed 42 cooperation agreements, extended their 25-year friendship treaty, and issued a joint rejection of "a return to a world order where only force prevails."

Xi called the relationship "at the highest level in their history." Both leaders condemned US and Israeli attacks on Iran and called for immediate dialogue.

The unipolar fantasy is over. The rest of the world is moving on.

🇲🇽🏭 TORTILLA PRICES STABLE THROUGH END OF 2026

The Consejo Nacional de la Tortilla confirms no further price increases expected through year-end. The average national price sits at 24.27 pesos/kg — up just 37 centavos since January.

CNT president Homero López García credits strategic alliances with gas suppliers and machinery manufacturers keeping costs down. Corn prices remain below historical levels.

Food price stability is not an accident — it is policy.

The man the US once celebrated as Mexico's top cop keeps getting more expensive to clean up after.

🇲🇽🚆 MEXICO PLANS 2,377 KM OF NEW RAIL — CALDERÓN BUILT 65

The numbers: Calderón built 65 km of rail in 6 years. Peña Nieto managed 187 km. AMLO delivered 1,736 km. Now Sheinbaum plans 2,377 km more — CDMX-Pachuca, CDMX-Querétaro, Querétaro-Irapuato, Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo.

88,559 tons of rail under contract. Military engineers have completed 800 km of route planning. First steel deliveries already arriving in Saltillo. 27.2 million square meters of right-of-way liberated.

"The difference is not just kilometers — it is a distinct vision of public infrastructure and mobility," says transport agency director Andrés Lajous.

🇲🇽🏭 US SHUT THE BORDER TO MEXICAN CATTLE — MEXICO ADAPTED

When the US closed its border to Mexican livestock over screwworm in November 2024, the hit was massive: 1.8 million head blocked, $1.85 billion in losses.

But Mexico's livestock sector did not collapse. It pivoted. Processed meat exports to the US surged 20% in Q1 2026 as the industry moved up the value chain. The sector now aims to double beef exports next year.

Washington closes a door. Mexico builds a processing plant.

🔥🇲🇽 FGR: SINALOA CARTEL INFILTRATED 8 MORELOS MUNICIPALITIES THROUGH CAMPAIGN FINANCING

Mexico's Attorney General reveals the Sinaloa Cartel penetrated at least 8 Morelos municipalities by financing political campaigns and intimidating opponents. A sitting mayor, a former mayor, and 4 municipal officials arrested. The UIF froze 32 accounts — individuals and shell companies tied to cartel operator Júpiter Araujo "El Barbas."

A leaked 2025 video shows mayors of Atlatlahuacán and Cuautla meeting directly with the cartel. This is what dismantling narco-political networks looks like: follow the money, arrest the officials, freeze the assets.

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO'S ECONOMY GROWS 0.3% IN APRIL — INDUSTRY BOUNCES BACK AFTER TARIFF SHOCK

INEGI's leading indicator (IOAE) shows Mexico's economy grew 0.3% monthly in April. Industry reversed March's -0.6% contraction to post +0.3%, while services held steady at 0.3%. Year-over-year growth hit 0.3%, with services advancing 0.7% annually.

Not spectacular — but the signal matters: Mexico's industrial sector absorbed the initial tariff hit and bounced back in a single month. Services remain the anchor keeping the broader economy moving forward.
